text:
I have two kids - a two year old and a baby, and we’ve never experienced anything to do with them not being Jewish. My son had a Brit (done by doctors). In gan, they do kabbalat shabbat every week and he is regularly made the ‘aba’ of shabbat. I think as the others say, it depends on the community/area where you choose to build a family. 
Obviously they will not be able to get married through the rabbinut if things continue as they are today.. But then again, most of our secular friends preferred not to get married through the rabbinut even if they are Jewish anyway.
In this group, most of the couples where the woman is the foreigner will be in your situation - since them not being jewish is precisely why they need to go through the gradual process. So we are not alone, we are a bit community all experiencing the same☺️
In my opinion, we all experience some point in our lives where we will feel ‘different’ anyway or are treated differently. The most important thing is that I can teach my children what to do in these circumstances and be confident in who they are. I wouldn’t want my children to ever change themselves for anybody else so why would I convert to become someone I’m not? 
Good luck!
